records.name: Luv-N-Bunns Rabbit Rescue
records.summary: A rabbit rescue that takes in domestic rabbits from shelters, strays, and hoarding cases and places them in foster and adoptive homes in the Philadelphia area. It also arranges veterinary care and holds rabbit care outreach events.
records.what_you_do: Foster a rabbit until it is adopted, volunteer through the application on the site, or adopt after an emailed application and screening.

schedule.text: Adoptions usually happen at a weekend adoption day after an approved application. No dates are posted on the site.

cost.text: Adoption fee not stated on the site. Each surrender asks for a $65 donation.

first_step.how: Email volunteer@luvnbunns.org to ask about volunteer roles, or email bunnies@luvnbunns.org to ask for a foster or adoption application
first_step.basis: Adoption and fostering start with an application that is reviewed before you can meet any rabbit, and the site describes no public visiting day.
first_step.what_to_expect: The rabbits live in private foster homes, so there is no public place to visit them, and the first contact is by email. Adoption happens on a weekend adoption day after your application is approved, and you take your rabbit home that same day. The rescue says fostering is its biggest need, and it also asks for help with vet transport, events, and care at its adoption center.
first_visit_tips: Have a pet carrier and your home set up before adoption day, since you take the rabbit home the same day.
Expect email replies to take a few days, so start early.
If you plan to bring a child under 18 to the adoption center, tell the rescue first.

records.notes: The contact page says the rescue has no physical location and no place to visit the animals, while the volunteer page describes a new adoption center in Huntingdon Valley, PA (outside the city) and vet transport to Wayne, PA. The only location kept is the IRS mailing address in Philadelphia 19115. Surrender intake is about three to four months behind, and the home page counters show zero adoptions for 2026 and zero intake requests for 2025 and 2026 to date, which may be stale. Adoption fee is not stated. No dated item on the site; the foster guide file is labeled 2022, so status is a judgement from a working site with no dates.

records.name: NE Phila Connected
records.summary: A neighborhood group in Northeast Philadelphia that runs a town watch and helps residents, including immigrant and limited-English speakers, find local resources. It also holds information meetings on local programs and laws.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the town watch, come to an information meeting, or ask for help connecting with local services.

cost.text: Not stated on the site; the group asks for donations.

first_step.how: Call (844) 533-3362 and ask when the next town watch patrol or information meeting is, and where it meets.
first_step.basis: The site welcomes people of any background, but it gives no meeting dates, places or join steps; the way in is a phone call, a Facebook group, or a website account form.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit. From the About page, the core work is a town watch in which volunteers patrol streets, check on local businesses, and share information. The group also holds information meetings on local programs and laws and helps residents with limited English reach local services. The site does not say what taking part costs, though it asks for donations.
first_visit_tips: Call first, since the site lists no meeting times or places.
Ask whether a town watch patrol or an information meeting is the best first step for you.

records.notes: The only dated items are the group's own 2020 start (May 27, 2020) and its June 22, 2020 town watch registration. The 2026 footer is not evidence. A strict dated-evidence reading would make this group dormant; status is kept at probably_active from tier 1 as a judgement and should be confirmed by phone. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because the only clear route is a phone call and no meeting dates or places are published. No languages are named on the site. The Facebook group was not used as a source.

records.name: Action for Justice Collective
records.summary: A youth nonprofit that runs a school-based mentoring program and works with partners on a gaming and esports program for youth affected by gun violence. Its site also lists a partner program for young women ages 12 to 21.
records.what_you_do: Young people take part in mentoring at schools, gaming and esports activities, and life skills or career exploration. Volunteers sign up through the group's volunteer page.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer application at afjcollective.org/become-a-volunteer or email volunteers@afjcollective.org, and say which youth program you want to help.
first_step.basis: Volunteers apply, the team reviews the application, and then calls for an interview before any work starts. No schedule or sign-up steps for young people are posted.
first_step.what_to_expect: The page says anyone from any background or experience level can apply to volunteer, and that the group provides the training volunteers need. Before you start, you apply, the team reviews the application, and you are contacted for an interview. The site does not say how long a first shift lasts, where volunteers serve, or what a typical week looks like.
first_visit_tips: Be ready for an interview after you apply, and think about which kind of help you would like to give.
Email volunteers@afjcollective.org with questions about where you would serve, since the site does not say.

records.notes: The team page gives a suite address at the same building already listed, plus a support phone and email. The only dated item on the site is the 2020 founding. The Events page is a menu link with no content, so it gives no event evidence. Status is kept at probably_active as a working site with no dates, but a strict dated-evidence reading would make it dormant; orchestrator to decide. Ages for the youth programs are not stated, so crowd is kept from tier 1. The school names for the mentoring program are not given. Background check, Act 153 clearance and youth-contact rules are not on the site, so they are left out. Contact name corrected from a typo ('Michael a Brown') to 'Michael Brown' per the team page. Partner programs are in leads_only.

records.name: ATTRACT Philly
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit for young people that runs mentoring and leadership programs, including literacy, mock job interviews, and a scholarship. It also runs service events such as a toy drive and a movie night.
records.what_you_do: Join a signature program such as Born to Lead, Literacy for Leaders, or Queen's Code, take part in a service event, or ask about volunteering or an internship.

first_step.how: Email attract.philly@gmail.com and ask which program has open registration now: Born to Lead (boys ages 10 to 16), Queen's Code (girls ages 10 to 16), or Literacy for Leaders (Pre-K through fifth grade).
first_step.basis: The program pages give ages and a 10-week format, but the registration and history dates we found are from 2016 and 2019 and no current sign-up dates are posted, so the way in for a young person is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Born to Lead and Queen's Code are 10-week mentoring programs for boys and girls ages 10 to 16. Queen's Code adds information sessions on life skills and service projects. Literacy for Leaders is a reading program for children from Pre-K through fifth grade. The site does not say where or when sessions meet, or what they cost now, so ask before you plan a visit.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the meeting place and times before you go, since the program pages do not list them.
If you want to volunteer instead, use the volunteer form on the site, which asks for your contact details and a position.

records.notes: The Born to Lead page shows a registration banner dated 2019, and the Queen's Code page says the program started in May 2016, so those pages may be out of date. Born to Lead registration runs through an outside booking page that was not opened. The Literacy for Leaders page lists no dates. The request program form needs at least 10 participants per program and at least two weeks' notice. The newest dated item is a May 7, 2025 scholarship post, which sets last_sign_of_life. The mock interview and Sky's the Limit pages were not opened. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because current sign-up is unclear. Crowd corrected from teens and young adults to kids, teens and young adults. The P.O. Box from the site is added, and a duplicate IRS entry is dropped.

records.name: Black Science Coalition and Institute
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit whose board is made up of Black scientists and science supporters. It makes a science podcast and a magazine, holds photo and story contests on everyday science, and runs science journalism workshops.
records.what_you_do: Listen to the B-Scientists podcast or read the magazine on B-Scientists.com. The 2026 photo and story contest had entries due Sept. 25, 2026; the page says that deadline may be extended, and winners are announced in November.

cost.text: Free to browse. Donating is optional, and the shop sells merchandise.

first_step.how: Listen to the B-Scientists podcast, then email contactus@thebsci.org to ask about the next online workshop or info session.
first_step.basis: The public way in is listening, reading and attending events, but the site does not say how to join a chapter or take part as a member.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most of the group is online: a podcast, a magazine on B-Scientists.com, and workshops on science journalism and video, some held online and at least one listed in Philadelphia. The events page lists dates without years and gives no times, costs or sign-up steps, so email before you plan to attend. The 2026 photo and story contest, now past its entry deadline, was open only to U.S.-based scientists, storytellers and journalists.
first_visit_tips: Email contactus@thebsci.org for event times, costs and how to register, since the events page does not list them.
Start with the podcast to get a feel for the group before you attend an event.

records.notes: As of this check (2026-10-08) the contest entry deadline of Sept. 25, 2026 has passed. The page says it may be extended; no extension was visible. The events page gives dates with no years, so it is not used as dated evidence and no year was assigned to any event. The chapter page explains how to start a chapter but not how to join one, and it names the chapters B-SCI Philly, B-SCI Georgia and B-SCI USC. Podcast page gives no platforms, episode dates or cost. Contest needs a Google sign-in to upload and allows one entry per person. Newcomer rating kept at 2.

records.name: Bringing Everybody Together
records.summary: A community group for young people that runs an after school homework program, a youth program called Lady BET, a chess program, and a youth-led online talk show.
records.what_you_do: Join the after school program at the Logan PAL Center, apply to Lady BET with a recommendation letter, or ask about the chess program or the youth-led talk show. Use the contact form to ask which program fits and how to sign up.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us form on mybetfamily.com to ask which after school or youth program has openings now, and how to sign up.
first_step.basis: The after school program is described in plain terms, but the site gives no days, times, ages or sign-up steps, Lady BET needs an application and a recommendation letter, and the only contact route is a form.
first_step.what_to_expect: The after school program offers homework help, tutoring, computer access, and a set place to study. It also gives a supervised place for kids to wait until a parent gets home, and students can bring a friend. Teachers can refer students who are struggling or need to stay after school, and they can ask for proof of attendance.
first_visit_tips: Ask the contact form for days, times and cost before you go, since the site does not list them.
For Lady BET, ask how to get the BET youth application and the adult recommendation letter form.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the site is an event dated 11/28/2020 (Evenings in the Park at Estuary Park). Other dates are copyright footers, which do not count. Status is kept at probably_active from tier 1 because the program pages describe current services, but a strict dated-evidence reading would make this dormant; orchestrator to decide. The Logan PAL Center address comes from the after school page with no ZIP or city; in_city is set from the group's Philadelphia address. The after school page gives no ages, days, times or cost. The Lady BET page does not say the program is for girls, so no gender is stated. The Royal-T Chess page shows only its menu name. Contact is a reCAPTCHA form with no public email or phone. The Support Our Youth page has unfinished placeholder text and no volunteer route; the form was not submitted.

records.name: Building Bridges In Greater Olney (B.B.G.O.)
records.summary: A neighborhood group the City of Philadelphia has registered to be consulted on zoning and development in the Upper North part of the city, Building Bridges In Greater Olney (B.B.G.O.) gives neighbors a place to hear about projects and respond.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over.

first_step.how: Email bbgo19120@gmail.com to ask when the next meeting on zoning and development is, and how to join the online call for it.

records.notes: No website of its own was found. The only public presence named is an Instagram account, which was not used as a source for facts. A web search found no sources about the group. The city registry record lists the organization, its primary contact and its meeting address, with an expiration year of 2028 and no effective date. Tier 1 recorded active status and a 2026-10 date; neither could be traced to a dated item on this pass, so status is set to unknown and last_sign_of_life is removed. The city record also lists an online meeting link, which is not copied here; ask by email for it. The phone number is the primary contact as the city lists it. Newcomer rating and what to expect are left out for lack of evidence.

leads_only.note: Named on the Action for Justice Collective site as a program for young women ages 12 to 21, described there as a nonprofit. Its own site was not checked.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Gaming Initiative (PGI)
leads_only.note: Named on the Action for Justice Collective site as a gaming and esports program for youth affected by gun violence, run with a partner. Its own site was not checked.

leads_only.name: Institute of African American Youth (IDAAY)
leads_only.note: Named on the Action for Justice Collective site as the partner that runs the gaming program with it. Its own site was not checked.

notes: Batch 019, 7 groups, all written at research_tier 2. Verdicts: publish 7, hide 0, not_a_group 0, duplicate 0, out_of_area 0. Searches: 1 of 1 used (no useful results for Building Bridges In Greater Olney). Fetches: 35 of 60. No blocks or rate limiting. Three groups (NE Phila Connected, Action for Justice Collective, Bringing Everybody Together) have no dated item newer than 2020 apart from footers and dated program pages; status is kept at probably_active under the working-site rule, but a strict dated-evidence reading would make them dormant. Building Bridges In Greater Olney has no website of its own, so status is unknown. Born to Lead (2019 banner) and Queen's Code (2016) pages look outdated. Corrections to tier 1: ATTRACT Philly crowd and ages, NE Phila Connected newcomer rating 3 to 2, Action for Justice Collective contact name and office address, Black Science Coalition contest now past its deadline, Building Bridges status and meeting link. The site-wide dash rule was applied to all text.
